correctness.rationale: For K_p square K_q (2<=p<=q), an empty row/column forces weight >=2p; otherwise all row/column supports are nonempty, changing every label two to one lowers weight without invalidating positive support or zero-site two-neighbor requirements. The associated bipartite incidence graph then has no isolated vertices or single-edge component. With c<=min(p,floor((p+q)/3)), at least p+q-c edges are needed, and a spanning forest construction attains that bound. For p=q=n, ceil(4n/3)<2n, so every optimum has no twos, and equality forces a forest with floor(2n/3) components of order>=3. The bipartite Cayley tree count a^(b-1)b^(a-1) plus excess-vertex profiles (all size3, one size4, or one size5/two size4) derives the three rational closed formulas, including n=2 boundary. Independently checked all labelings for five rectangular boards and coefficient-DP counts n=2..10.
